register.question: how much dispatch buffer / safety stock should operations plan
register.decision: commit next-day dispatch capacity and dock slots at the point forecast plus the 95% prediction interval upper bound
register.trigger_metric: next-day ridge demand forecast (lag-1 features; multi-day horizons not validated)
register.trigger_threshold: capacity buffer = forecast + 1.96 * residual sd (half-width 6.8 shipments/day)
register.action: reserve dock slots and dispatch staff against the 95% upper bound buffer

expected_impact_range.low: reduces under-capacity shortfall from 41.9 to 6.1 shipment-days (saving 35.8 shortfall units on test)
expected_impact_range.high: incurs 6.8 unused capacity units per day; break-even shortfall-to-unused cost ratio is 4.31:1

register.cost_of_wrong_call: under-planning causes spot freight expedite penalties ($150/unit); over-planning causes idle vehicle reservation waste ($30/unit)
register.data_required: daily order volumes history, next-day booking count and ridge lag-1 features

register.question: which at-risk shipments should an expeditor triage, and at what threshold
register.decision: escalate shipments whose late delivery risk score meets or exceeds the operational threshold of 0.05
register.trigger_metric: gradient boosting late delivery risk score
register.trigger_threshold: risk score >= 0.05 (justified over val-cost-optimal t*=0.50 which shuts triage off)
register.action: dispatch dedicated expeditor triage; escalate to carrier dispatch operations within 2 hours of flagging

expected_impact_range.low: catches 46.7% of late shipments (7 of 15, 95% CI 24.8% - 69.9%) at precision 11.7% (95% CI 5.8% - 22.2%)
expected_impact_range.high: generates $6,900 net policy saving ($15,600 vs $22,500 no-triage; 95% bootstrap CI $0 - $14,641)

register.cost_of_wrong_call: false negative (missed late) costs $1,500 contractual breach; false positive (wasted triage) costs $60 expeditor time
register.data_required: booking features (mode, origin, destination, weight, category, order-to-ship lag)
register.review_cadence: daily triage queue refresh; threshold and sensitivity review quarterly

register.question: where should service effort and capacity be concentrated across carriers and lanes
register.decision: maintain mode-specific delivery promises and place underperforming carrier lanes on structured remediation plans
register.trigger_metric: lane-level on-time delivery rate for carrier-lane pairs with at least 20 shipments
register.trigger_threshold: carrier lane on-time rate below 95% (extract carrier gap is 6.5 percentage points between ocean and non-ocean)
register.action: issue formal corrective action requests for ocean carriers (Kestrel 93.5%, Poseidon 94.6%); divert urgent cargo to air

expected_impact_range.low: remediates ocean transit variance (5.4% to 6.5% late rate on ocean vs 0% on road/air)
expected_impact_range.high: protects high-value lanes (e.g. UK to US ocean, 81.8% on-time, n=22, 95% CI 61.5% - 92.7%)

register.cost_of_wrong_call: penalising carriers without sufficient sample size (violating Wilson interval bounds)
register.data_required: carrier-lane shipment logs, delivery confirmations, and segment sample counts

register.question: when should the models be retrained and the operational decisions re-visited
register.decision: trigger immediate automated retraining when forecast interval coverage or feature drift crosses numeric thresholds
register.trigger_metric: rolling 28-day 95% forecast interval coverage and population stability index (PSI) on features
register.trigger_threshold: empirical forecast coverage falls below 90% (nominal 95%) OR feature PSI > 0.20 (or KS p < 0.01)
register.action: re-fit ridge and gradient boosting models on rolling window; re-derive optimal threshold and sensitivity grid

expected_impact_range.low: prevents operational actions based on stale seasonal patterns or shifted mode distributions
expected_impact_range.high: ensures triage budget remains cost-positive under evolving carrier performance

register.cost_of_wrong_call: deploying a drifted model degrades triage precision below break-even ratio (8.57:1), causing net financial loss
register.data_required: daily actual shipment volumes, realized delivery timestamps, input feature logs
register.review_cadence: continuous automated telemetry monitoring with monthly executive review

forecast.horizon_scope: next-day ahead dispatch planning; longer multi-day horizons not validated
forecast.model_policy: next-day point forecast + 95% prediction interval upper bound

triage.justification: Threshold t=0.05 is recommended over validation cost-optimal t*=0.50. On validation (n=620, 8 late), both thresholds yield TP=0, so validation expected cost prefers t*=0.50 solely by suppressing all alarms (flagging 5 vs 42). On test (n=851, 15 late), t*=0.50 yields 0% recall (0/15) and -$600 net loss, whereas t=0.05 catches 46.7% (7/15) of late shipments and saves $6,900 net.
